rounds.fact: Funny or Die launched in 2007 co-founded by Will Ferrell, and its debut video 'The Landlord' became one of the most-watched comedy videos of the early web-video era.
Wired magazine's website carried over its distinctive, colorful print design into the browser, standing out at a time when most news sites still looked like plain digital newspapers.
ICQ (a pun on 'I seek you') launched in 1996 and is widely credited as the first mass-market instant messaging program, complete with its now-iconic 'uh-oh' message sound.
Tripod was a major free website-builder alongside GeoCities and Angelfire, and was eventually bought by Lycos as part of its portal strategy in the late 90s.
Match.com launched in 1995 and is one of the very first online dating sites, predating the smartphone-app dating era by almost two decades.
